title: Project curation outlives memory qualification or issuing service at dispatch and cursor commit
cause: An initial memory authorization does not cover asynchronous catalog/model/tool work or a queued cursor. Generic model execute permission can remain valid after memory qualification is withdrawn. Replacing the captured execution issuer must not lend another actor or permission.
implementation: Curation retains the original issuer and captured participants through instance-owned AsyncLocalStorage. Current-service identity and memory qualification recheck before rounds, after responses, after capacity admission and at physical adapter dispatch. Cursor authorization runs inside the serialized write queue after storage waits and returns a synchronous final issuer/scope/availability guard. Cancellation checks and existing cleanup/permits remain owned. The context is disabled only after all captured tasks settle.
